chapters.title: Visions of God
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 1

1And it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was among the exiles by the river Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

2On the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile,

3the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the LORD was on him there.

The Living Creatures

4I looked: a storm wind was coming out of the north, a great cloud with fire flashing through it and brightness all around it, and from the middle of it, from the middle of the fire, something like the gleam of amber.

5From the middle of it came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had the likeness of a human.

6Each had four faces, and each of them had four wings.

7Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the sole of a calf's foot; and they sparkled like the gleam of burnished bronze.

8They had human hands under their wings on their four sides. As for the faces and wings of the four of them,

9their wings touched one another. They did not turn as they went; each went straight ahead.

10As for the likeness of their faces, each of the four had the face of a human, and on the right the face of a lion, and on the left the face of an ox, and each of the four had the face of an eagle.

11Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above: each had two wings touching those of another, and two covering their bodies.

12Each went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they went, without turning as they went.

13As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. Fire moved back and forth among the living creatures; the fire was bright, and lightning went out of the fire.

14The living creatures darted back and forth like the appearance of a flash of lightning.

The Wheels

15As I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each of the living creatures, for each of their four faces.

16The appearance of the wheels and their making was like the gleam of beryl, and all four had one likeness; their appearance and their making were as if a wheel were inside a wheel.

17When they went, they went in any of their four directions, without turning as they went.

18As for their rims, they were high and fearsome, and the rims of all four were full of eyes all around.

19When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the living creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose.

20Wherever the spirit would go, they went, wherever the spirit went, and the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

21When those went, these went; when those stood still, these stood still; and when those rose from the ground, the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

The Throne

22Over the heads of the living creature was the likeness of an expanse, like the gleam of awe-inspiring crystal, spread out over their heads above.

23Under the expanse their wings were stretched out straight, one toward another. Each had two that covered its body on one side, and each had two that covered it on the other side.

24When they went, I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a sound of tumult like the sound of an army. When they stood still, they let down their wings.

25A voice came from above the expanse that was over their heads; when they stood still, they let down their wings.

26Above the expanse that was over their heads was something like the appearance of sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne; and on the likeness of the throne, high above it, was a likeness like the appearance of a human.

27I saw something like the gleam of amber, like the appearance of fire enclosed all around, from the appearance of His waist upward; and from the appearance of His waist downward I saw something like the appearance of fire, and there was brightness all around Him.

28Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on a day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. That was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "in the thirtieth year… the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile" — two dates, and the first is not said to be of anything: the book never says what the thirtieth year counts from. The second is the exiles' own count, from the year the king was taken to Babylon (2 Kings 24:12–15). The prophet speaks as I in v1, and v3 names him in the third person, Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest.

  • v3 "the hand of the LORD was on him there" — Ezekiel's words for being seized by the LORD. The hand comes on him again at 3:14 and 3:22, each time before he is moved or shown something.

  • vv4, 27 "something like the gleam of amber" — chashmal, found only in Ezekiel (here, v27 and 8:2). What it names is not known. The Greek has ēlektron, its word both for amber and for a shining alloy of gold and silver. The English takes the first; either way it is something that glows in the fire.

  • vv5, 10 "four living creatures… the face of a human… a lion… an ox… an eagle" — chayyot, plain "living things." The book names them later: he sees them again by the river Chebar and knew that they were cherubim (10:20), and there the face of the ox is called the face of a cherub (10:14).

  • v14, v24 "darted back and forth… like the voice of the Almighty, a sound of tumult like the sound of an army" — the Greek has neither: no v14, and in v24 only like the sound of much water. Shaddai, the Almighty, appears here for the first time in the book.

  • v22 "the likeness of an expanse… spread out over their heads" — raqia, the word of the second day: Let there be a beaten expanse in the middle of the waters (Genesis 1:6). In Genesis it holds back the waters above; here it carries the throne.

  • v26 "something like the appearance of sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne" — what the elders saw at Sinai, under His feet was something like brickwork of sapphire (Exodus 24:10). Ezekiel sees the stone again, and now a throne on it.

  • v28 "Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on a day of rain" — the bow of the covenant with Noah, My bow I have set in the cloud (Genesis 9:13).

  • v28 "the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD" — the chapter piles up two words, mar'eh, "appearance," and demut, "likeness," more than twenty times, and never once says that Ezekiel saw the LORD. At the top of it all is the appearance of the likeness of the glory, three steps removed, and that is where he falls on his face.

chapters.title: Son of Man
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 2

1He said to me, "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."

2As He spoke to me, the spirit entered me and set me on my feet, and I heard Him speaking to me.

3He said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the sons of Israel, to rebellious nations that have rebelled against Me. They and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day.

4The sons are hard-faced and hard-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.'

5As for them, whether they hear or refuse — for they are a rebellious house — they will know that a prophet has been among them.

6As for you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are around you and you live among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their looks, for they are a rebellious house.

7You shall speak My words to them, whether they hear or refuse, for they are rebellious.

8But you, son of man, hear what I am saying to you: do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."

9I looked: a hand was stretched out to me, and in it was a scroll.

10He spread it out before me, and it was written on the front and on the back; and written on it were laments and mourning and woe.

Notes

  • v1 "Son of man" — ben adam, "son of a human," a member of humankind. It is God's name for Ezekiel throughout the book, and it comes first just after the vision of a likeness like the appearance of a human on the throne (1:26). The one on the throne only looks like a human; the one on the ground is one.

  • v2 "the spirit entered me and set me on my feet" — ruach, with no of the LORD and no article: the word of the storm wind (1:4) and of the spirit that moved the living creatures and the wheels (1:12, 20). What drove the creatures now enters the man and stands him up. It lifts him again at 3:12 and 3:14.

  • v3 "to rebellious nations" — goyim, the word for the nations, said here of Israel. The rest of the chapter has a name for them, a rebellious house (vv5, 6, 8), and the book keeps it (3:9, 26, 27).

  • v4 "hard-faced and hard-hearted" — qeshei fanim ve-chizqei lev. The second word is the root of Ezekiel's own name, Yechezqel, "God makes strong," and 3:7–9 turns on it.

  • vv5, 7 "whether they hear or refuse" — the commission does not depend on being heard. Its only promised result is they will know that a prophet has been among them.

  • v6 "briers and thorns… scorpions" — sarabim, found only here, and sallonim, found again only at 28:24; both are taken as thorny plants from the context.

  • vv8–10 "eat what I am giving you… a scroll" — Jeremiah said, Your words were found, and I ate them (Jeremiah 15:16); for Ezekiel the eating is not a figure, and the next chapter tells it.

  • v10 "written on the front and on the back" — like the tablets at Sinai, written on both their sides, on one side and on the other (Exodus 32:15). Both sides are full, and all of it is laments and mourning and woe.

chapters.title: A Watchman for the House of Israel
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 3

1He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you find. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel."

2So I opened my mouth, and He gave me this scroll to eat.

3He said to me, "Son of man, feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll that I am giving you." So I ate it, and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.

4He said to me, "Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak My words to them.

5For you are not being sent to a people of speech too deep to understand and of heavy tongue, but to the house of Israel;

6not to many peoples of speech too deep to understand and of heavy tongue, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.

7But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to Me; for all the house of Israel are hard-browed and hard-hearted.

8I have made your face as hard as their faces, and your brow as hard as their brows.

9Like diamond, harder than flint, I have made your brow. Do not be afraid of them or dismayed by their looks, for they are a rebellious house."

10He said to me, "Son of man, all My words that I speak to you, take into your heart and hear with your ears.

11Go to the exiles, to the sons of your people, and speak to them and say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says,' whether they hear or refuse."

12Then the spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from His place!"

13It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, the sound of a great rumbling.

14The spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went bitter, in the heat of my spirit, and the hand of the LORD was strong on me.

15I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who lived by the river Chebar. I sat where they were sitting, and I sat there seven days among them, stunned.

The Watchman

16And it came to pass at the end of seven days that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

17"Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. When you hear a word from My mouth, you shall warn them from Me.

18When I say to the wicked, 'You shall surely die,' and you do not warn him or speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way to save his life, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but his blood I will require from your hand.

19But if you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness or from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life.

20When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he shall die. Because you did not warn him, he shall die in his sin, and the righteous deeds he has done shall not be remembered; but his blood I will require from your hand.

21But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live, because he took warning; and you will have saved your life."

Bound and Silent

22The hand of the LORD was on me there, and He said to me, "Get up, go out into the plain, and there I will speak with you."

23So I got up and went out into the plain, and the glory of the LORD was standing there, like the glory I had seen by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face.

24Then the spirit entered me and set me on my feet, and He spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself inside your house.

25As for you, son of man, they will put cords on you and bind you with them, so that you cannot go out among them.

26I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, and you will be mute and unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious house.

27But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.' Whoever will hear, let him hear; and whoever refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house."

Notes

  • v3 "in my mouth it was as sweet as honey" — the words of the psalm, sweeter than honey to my mouth (Psalm 119:103), though the scroll was written with laments and mourning and woe (2:10). In v14 he goes away bitter.

  • vv5–6 "a people of speech too deep to understand and of heavy tongue" — imqei safah ve-khivdei lashon. Isaiah used the first for the foreign invader, the people of a speech too deep to understand (Isaiah 33:19); the second is Moses' word for himself, heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue (Exodus 4:10). Israel speaks Ezekiel's language, and that is the trouble: foreigners would have listened.

  • vv7–9, 14 "hard-browed… I have made your face as hard as their faces… the hand of the LORD was strong on me" — chazaq, "hard, strong," four times in three verses and again in v14: the root of Yechezqel, "God makes strong." The people are hard; God makes the prophet harder, like diamond, harder than flint. Shamir, "diamond," is Jeremiah's word for the point that writes Judah's sin, with a point of diamond it is engraved (Jeremiah 17:1).

  • vv12–13 "the sound of a great rumbling: 'Blessed be the glory of the LORD from His place!'" — ra'ash, the word for an earthquake. The Greek also reads Blessed. What he hears behind him is the vision of chapter 1 moving off: the wings of the living creatures and the wheels.

  • v15 "I sat there seven days among them, stunned" — mashmim, appalled, struck silent, as Job's friends sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him (Job 2:13).

  • vv17–21 "I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel" — tsofeh, the man on the wall who sees what is coming. God had said to Israel through Jeremiah, I set watchmen over you (Jeremiah 6:17); now one man is set, and his own life hangs on whether he gives warning. The charge is given again in the same words at 33:7–9.

  • v20 "I lay a stumbling block before him" — mikhshol, Jeremiah's word, I am about to lay stumbling blocks before this people (Jeremiah 6:21). The stumbling block is God's; the warning is the prophet's.

  • vv25–27 "they will put cords on you… you will be mute… But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth" — the prophet is bound and silent except when God speaks through him. The silence is lifted when word comes that the city has fallen (24:27; 33:22).

chapters.title: The Siege on a Brick
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 4

1"As for you, son of man, take a brick and set it before you, and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem.

2Lay siege against it: build a siege wall against it, heap up a ramp against it, set camps against it, and place battering rams against it all around.

3As for you, take an iron griddle and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face toward it, and it will be under siege, and you shall besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.

4As for you, lie on your left side and lay the guilt of the house of Israel on it. For the number of days that you lie on it, you shall carry their guilt.

5I have assigned you the years of their guilt as a number of days, three hundred and ninety days; so you shall carry the guilt of the house of Israel.

6When you have completed these, you shall lie a second time, on your right side, and carry the guilt of the house of Judah forty days, a day for each year, a day for each year; I have assigned it to you.

7You shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem with your arm bared, and you shall prophesy against it.

8I will put cords on you, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.

9As for you, take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and spelt, put them in one vessel, and make bread of them for yourself. For the number of days that you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days, you shall eat it.

10The food you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; you shall eat it at set times.

11You shall drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; you shall drink it at set times.

12You shall eat it as a barley cake, baking it on human dung in their sight."

13The LORD said, "This is how the sons of Israel will eat their bread unclean among the nations where I will drive them."

14Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I have never been made unclean. From my youth until now I have never eaten an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts, and no foul meat has ever entered my mouth."

15He said to me, "See, I give you cow dung instead of human dung, and you shall prepare your bread on it."

16He said to me, "Son of man, I am about to break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in horror,

17so that they will lack bread and water, and look at one another in horror, and rot away in their guilt."

Notes

  • vv1–3 "take a brick… engrave on it a city, Jerusalem… an iron griddle… as an iron wall" — the prophet acts out the siege in miniature: a clay brick for the city, siege works around it, and an iron griddle set up as a wall between the prophet and the city. He is to set his face toward it, the face God has just made hard (3:8–9).

  • vv4–6 "three hundred and ninety days… forty days, a day for each year" — the sentence in the wilderness counted the other way: By the number of the days you scouted out the land, forty days — a year for each day — you shall carry your guilt forty years (Numbers 14:34). Here the years of guilt are lived out as days, and carry the guilt is the same phrase. The Greek has one hundred and ninety days in vv5 and 9.

  • v4 "lay the guilt of the house of Israel on it… you shall carry their guilt" — nasa avon, the law's phrase for bearing the guilt of a wrong (Leviticus 7:18; 17:16). The prophet carries the people's guilt in his own body, lying on one side for more than a year.

  • v8 "I will put cords on you" — the cords that the people will put on him (3:25), God now puts on him Himself.

  • vv9–11 "twenty shekels a day… a sixth of a hin" — starvation rations: bread of whatever grains are left, mixed in one jar, eaten by weight, and water by the measure. At set times, literally "from time to time": at fixed intervals, not when he is hungry.

  • v14 "Ah, Lord GOD! I have never been made unclean" — the cry Jeremiah made at his call, Ah, Lord GOD! I do not know how to speak (Jeremiah 1:6). The priest protests by the law he has kept: an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts (Leviticus 17:15), and piggul, foul meat (Leviticus 7:18). God gives way on the dung, not on the hunger.

  • vv16–17 "I am about to break the staff of bread… They will eat bread by weight… and rot away in their guilt" — the curse of the law, word for word: When I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and ration it out by weight (Leviticus 26:26), and they will rot away in their guilt (26:39).

"As for you, son of man, take a brick and set it before you, and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem.
Lay siege against it: build a siege wall against it, heap up a ramp against it, set camps against it, and place battering rams against it all around.

As for you, take an iron griddle and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face toward it, and it will be under siege, and you shall besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.
As for you, lie on your left side and lay the guilt of the house of Israel on it. For the number of days that you lie on it, you shall carry their guilt.
I have assigned you the years of their guilt as a number of days, three hundred and ninety days; so you shall carry the guilt of the house of Israel.

When you have completed these, you shall lie a second time, on your right side, and carry the guilt of the house of Judah forty days, a day for each year, a day for each year; I have assigned it to you.
You shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem with your arm bared, and you shall prophesy against it.
I will put cords on you, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.

As for you, take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and spelt, put them in one vessel, and make bread of them for yourself. For the number of days that you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days, you shall eat it.
The food you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; you shall eat it at set times.
You shall drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; you shall drink it at set times.
You shall eat it as a barley cake, baking it on human dung in their sight."
The LORD said, "This is how the sons of Israel will eat their bread unclean among the nations where I will drive them."

Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I have never been made unclean. From my youth until now I have never eaten an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts, and no foul meat has ever entered my mouth."
He said to me, "See, I give you cow dung instead of human dung, and you shall prepare your bread on it."
He said to me, "Son of man, I am about to break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in horror,
so that they will lack bread and water, and look at one another in horror, and rot away in their guilt."

chapters.title: A Third, a Third and a Third
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 5

1"As for you, son of man, take a sharp sword; use it as a barber's razor, and pass it over your head and your beard. Then take scales for weighing, and divide the hair.

2A third you shall burn in the fire inside the city when the days of the siege are completed. A third you shall take and strike with the sword all around it. A third you shall scatter to the wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.

3Take from there a few, a small number, and bind them in the hem of your garment.

4Of these again you shall take some, throw them into the fire and burn them in the fire; from it a fire will go out to all the house of Israel.

5This is what the Lord GOD says: This is Jerusalem. I have set her in the middle of the nations, with countries all around her.

6She has rebelled against My judgments more wickedly than the nations, and against My statutes more than the countries around her; for they have rejected My judgments and have not walked in My statutes.

7Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have been more unruly than the nations around you, and have not walked in My statutes or kept My judgments, and have not even acted by the judgments of the nations around you,

8therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I Myself am against you, and I will carry out judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations.

9Because of all your detestable things I will do with you what I have never done, and the like of which I will never do again.

10Therefore fathers will eat their sons in your midst, and sons will eat their fathers. I will carry out judgments on you, and I will scatter all your remnant to every wind.

11Therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have made My sanctuary unclean with all your loathsome things and all your detestable things, I in turn will withdraw; My eye will not spare, and I in turn will have no pity.

12A third of you will die of pestilence and be consumed by famine in your midst; a third will fall by the sword around you; and a third I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.

13So My anger will be spent, and I will satisfy My wrath on them and be eased; and they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in My jealousy, when I have spent My wrath on them.

14I will make you a ruin and a reproach among the nations around you, in the sight of everyone who passes by.

15You will be a reproach and a taunt, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I carry out judgments on you in anger and in wrath and with furious rebukes. I, the LORD, have spoken.

16When I send against them the deadly arrows of famine, arrows for destruction, which I send to destroy you, I will bring more and more famine on you and break your staff of bread.

17I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will rob you of your children; pestilence and blood will pass through you, and I will bring the sword on you. I, the LORD, have spoken."

Notes

  • vv1–4 "take a sharp sword; use it as a barber's razor… divide the hair" — a priest was forbidden to shave his head or the edge of his beard (Leviticus 21:5). Ezekiel the priest shaves both with a sword, and the hair is the city: a third burned, a third cut down, a third scattered. Even the few kept back in his hem are not all safe.

  • v5 "I have set her in the middle of the nations" — Jerusalem's place among the nations is what makes her sin public. Every judgment in the chapter is done in the sight of the nations (v8), in the sight of everyone who passes by (v14).

  • v7 "and have not even acted by the judgments of the nations around you" — the Hebrew says not: Jerusalem has kept neither God's judgments nor even the laws of her neighbors. The Greek reads the same. At 11:12 the book says the opposite charge, that they acted by the judgments of the nations; each verse makes its own point.

  • v10 "fathers will eat their sons… and sons will eat their fathers" — the siege curse of the law (Leviticus 26:29; Deuteronomy 28:53), here turned both ways.

  • v13 "I will satisfy My wrath on them and be eased" — ve-hinnechamti, from nicham, the verb used for being comforted and for relenting. Here it is the relief of anger spent.

  • vv16–17 "break your staff of bread… wild beasts… rob you of your children… I will bring the sword on you" — the curses of Leviticus 26, in its words: When I break your staff of bread (26:26), they will rob you of your children (26:22), I will bring a sword on you (26:25). Ezekiel the priest preaches the end of the covenant from the covenant's own text.

chapters.title: To the Mountains of Israel
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 6

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them,

3and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys: I Myself am about to bring a sword on you, and I will destroy your high places.

4Your altars will be made desolate, your incense altars will be broken, and I will make your slain fall before your idols.

5I will lay the corpses of the sons of Israel before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

6In all your dwelling places the cities will be laid waste and the high places made desolate, so that your altars will be laid waste and bear their guilt, your idols will be broken and brought to an end, your incense altars cut down, and your works wiped out.

7The slain will fall in your midst, and you will know that I am the LORD.

8Yet I will leave a remnant, when you have some who escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered through the countries.

9Those of you who escape will remember Me among the nations where they are taken captive, how I was broken by their heart that gave itself to others and turned away from Me, and by their eyes that gave themselves to their idols. They will loathe themselves for the evils they have done, for all their detestable things.

10They will know that I am the LORD; I did not speak in vain of doing this harm to them.

11This is what the Lord GOD says: Strike with your hand and stamp with your foot, and say, 'Alas!' over all the evil detestable things of the house of Israel, who will fall by the sword, by famine and by pestilence.

12He who is far off will die of pestilence, he who is near will fall by the sword, and he who is left and is besieged will die of famine. So I will spend My wrath on them.

13You will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree and under every leafy oak, the places where they offered a soothing aroma to all their idols.

14I will stretch out My hand against them and make the land a desolation and a waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, in all their dwelling places; and they will know that I am the LORD."

Notes

  • vv3–6 "I will destroy your high places… your incense altars will be broken… I will make your slain fall before your idols" — the curse of the law, almost word for word: I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars, and throw your corpses on the corpses of your idols (Leviticus 26:30). Gillulim, "idols," is the law's word for them, and Ezekiel's word for them throughout the book.

  • vv7, 10, 13, 14 "you will know that I am the LORD" — the sentence that runs through the book, four times in this chapter alone. What the judgment is for is that it be known who is speaking.

  • v9 "how I was broken by their heart that gave itself to others" — nishbarti, "I was broken," God speaking of His own heart broken by theirs. The Greek has I have sworn, reading the same letters with one different (nishba'ti). The Hebrew is followed.

  • v9 "They will loathe themselves" — ve-naqottu bi-feneihem, "they will loathe in their own faces." The survivors' turning begins not with the land restored but with disgust at what they did.

  • v13 "the places where they offered a soothing aroma to all their idols" — re'ach nichoach, the law's phrase for the offering that pleases the LORD (Leviticus 1:9), given to idols on every hill. Where they offered it, their slain will lie.

  • v14 "from the wilderness to Diblah" — Diblatah, a place named only here; the Greek has the same name. The phrase seems to mark the land from end to end, but where Diblah was is not known.

chapters.title: The End Has Come
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 7

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"As for you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel:
An end! The end has come
on the four corners of the land.

3Now the end is on you,
and I will send My anger against you;
I will judge you according to your ways
and bring on you all your detestable things.

4My eye will not spare you, and I will have no pity;
I will bring your ways on you,
and your detestable things will be in your midst;
and you will know that I am the LORD.

5This is what the Lord GOD says:
Disaster, one disaster! It is coming!

6An end has come; the end has come;
it has awakened against you. It is coming!

7Your doom has come to you, you who live in the land.
The time has come; the day is near,
a day of tumult, and not of shouting on the mountains.

8Now soon I will pour out My wrath on you
and spend My anger on you;
I will judge you according to your ways
and bring on you all your detestable things.

9My eye will not spare, and I will have no pity;
I will bring on you according to your ways,
and your detestable things will be in your midst;
and you will know that I am the LORD who strikes.

10The day! It is coming!
Your doom has gone out;
the staff has put out blossoms; pride has sprouted.

11Violence has grown up into a staff of wickedness.
None of them, none of their multitude,
none of their wealth; no splendor among them.

12The time has come; the day has arrived.
Let the buyer not rejoice, nor the seller mourn,
for wrath is on all her multitude.

13For the seller will not return to what he sold,
even if they are still among the living;
for the vision concerning all her multitude will not be turned back,
and no one, in his iniquity, will hold on to his life.

14They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready,
but no one goes to battle,
for My wrath is on all her multitude.

15The sword is outside,
and pestilence and famine inside;
whoever is in the field will die by the sword,
and whoever is in the city, famine and pestilence will devour him.

16Even if their survivors escape,
they will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys,
all of them moaning, each for his iniquity.

17Every hand will hang limp,
and every knee will turn to water.

18They will put on sackcloth,
and horror will cover them;
shame will be on every face,
and baldness on all their heads.

19They will throw their silver into the streets,
and their gold will be an unclean thing;
their silver and their gold will not be able to rescue them
in the day of the LORD's fury.
They will not satisfy their hunger or fill their stomachs with it,
for it was the stumbling block of their iniquity.

20His beautiful ornament they turned to pride,
and made their detestable images, their loathsome things, out of it;
therefore I will make it an unclean thing to them.

21I will give it into the hands of strangers as plunder,
and to the wicked of the earth as spoil,
and they will profane it.

22I will turn My face from them,
and they will profane My treasured place;
robbers will enter it and profane it.

23Make the chain,
for the land is full of bloodshed
and the city is full of violence.

24I will bring the worst of the nations,
and they will take possession of their houses;
I will put an end to the pride of the strong,
and their holy places will be profaned.

25Anguish is coming;
they will seek peace, but there will be none.

26Disaster upon disaster will come,
and rumor upon rumor;
they will seek a vision from the prophet,
but the law will perish from the priest,
and counsel from the elders.

27The king will mourn,
the prince will be clothed in desolation,
and the hands of the people of the land will tremble.
According to their way I will deal with them,
and by their own judgments I will judge them;
and they will know that I am the LORD."

Notes

  • vv2–9 "An end! The end has come" — qets, five times in four verses, and in v6 a play on it: ha-qets heqits, "the end has awakened." The Greek gives these verses in another order and does not have the line about doom.

  • vv7, 10 "Your doom" — ha-tsefirah, a word whose sense here is not settled. Its only other use in the Bible is Isaiah's diadem of beauty (Isaiah 28:5), which does not fit the context; the English takes it from what the verses say around it, something that has come round to the land and gone out against it.

  • v10 "the staff has put out blossoms; pride has sprouted" — the words of Aaron's staff, which had sprouted. It had put out blossoms (Numbers 17:8): the same two verbs. There the blossoming staff proved the LORD's choice; here what blossoms is pride, and in v11 a staff of wickedness.

  • v11 "None of them, none of their multitude, none of their wealth; no splendor among them" — four short phrases with no verb, whose exact sense is uncertain. The Greek has a different line here. What is clear is that nothing of theirs is left.

  • vv12–13 "Let the buyer not rejoice, nor the seller mourn… the seller will not return to what he sold" — under the law, land sold went back to its family in the Jubilee: In this year of jubilee you shall return, each man to his holding (Leviticus 25:13). The end makes buying and selling meaningless; no one will be there to return.

  • vv19–20 "their gold will be an unclean thing… His beautiful ornament they turned to pride" — niddah, the word Lamentations used for the fallen city, Jerusalem has become an unclean thing among them (Lamentations 1:17). His ornament, edyo, is the word of Exodus 33:4, where the people mourned and no one put on his ornaments; whose ornament is meant here, the people's or God's, the verse does not say.

  • v22 "they will profane My treasured place" — tsefuni, "My hidden, treasured one." It is not named; with robbers will enter it, it is most naturally the temple.

  • v26 "but the law will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders" — the boast of Jeremiah's enemies turned around. They said, the law will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet (Jeremiah 18:18). Now it does, and they seek a vision from the prophet in vain.

chapters.title: Detestable Things in the House of the LORD
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 8

1And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was sitting in my house with the elders of Judah sitting before me, that the hand of the Lord GOD fell on me there.

2I looked: a likeness like the appearance of a man. From the appearance of His waist downward was fire, and from His waist upward something like the appearance of brightness, like the gleam of amber.

3He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my head; and the spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the seat of the image of jealousy was, which provokes jealousy.

4The glory of the God of Israel was there, like the vision I had seen in the plain.

5He said to me, "Son of man, lift up your eyes toward the north." So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and north of the altar gate, at the entrance, was this image of jealousy.

6He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they are doing, the great detestable things the house of Israel is committing here, to drive Me far from My sanctuary? But you will see still greater detestable things."

7He brought me to the entrance of the court, and I looked: there was a hole in the wall.

8He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and there was a doorway.

9He said to me, "Go in, and see the evil detestable things they are doing here."

10So I went in and looked: carved on the wall all around were every form of creeping thing and loathsome beast, and all the idols of the house of Israel.

11Seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel were standing before them, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them, each with his censer in his hand, and the fragrance of the cloud of incense was rising.

12He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in his room of images? For they say, 'The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.'"

13He said to me, "You will see still greater detestable things that they are doing."

14He brought me to the entrance of the gate of the house of the LORD that faces north, and there sat women weeping for Tammuz.

15He said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? You will see still greater detestable things than these."

16He brought me into the inner court of the house of the LORD, and at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, and they were bowing down to the sun toward the east.

17He said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? Is it too light a thing for the house of Judah to commit the detestable things they have committed here, that they must also fill the land with violence and provoke Me again and again? They are putting the branch to their nose.

18So I, too, will act in wrath; My eye will not spare, and I will have no pity. Though they cry in My ears with a loud voice, I will not listen to them."

Notes

  • v1 "in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day" — a year and two months after the call (1:1–2). The elders of Judah are sitting before him in his house in Babylon when he is taken to Jerusalem.

  • v2 "a likeness like the appearance of a man" — the Hebrew reads esh, "fire": a likeness like the appearance of fire. The Greek reads andros, "a man," the Hebrew ish, which differs from esh only in its vowels. The English follows the Greek, because the rest of the verse speaks of His waist, and this is the figure of 1:26–27, a likeness like the appearance of a human, with fire below the waist and amber above.

  • v3 "took me by a lock of my head" — tsitsit, the word for the tassels on the corners of the garment (Numbers 15:38), here the hair of his head.

  • vv3, 5 "the image of jealousy, which provokes jealousy" — semel, "image," the law's word in the form of any figure (Deuteronomy 4:16). The Song of Moses says it: They made Him jealous with strange gods (Deuteronomy 32:16). It stands at the gate, where the glory of the God of Israel is also standing (v4).

  • vv7–12 "dig through the wall… carved on the wall all around… each in his room of images" — seventy elders, the number of the elders who went up Sinai and saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24:9–10), burn incense in the dark to pictures on a wall. Among them is Jaazaniah son of Shaphan, of a family that stood by Jeremiah: the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah (Jeremiah 26:24).

  • v12 "The LORD does not see us" — they say it in a hidden room that the LORD is at that moment showing to His prophet.

  • v14 "women weeping for Tammuz" — ha-Tammuz, with the article; the Greek has Thammouz. The verse says no more than that he was mourned.

  • v16 "with their backs to the temple of the LORD… bowing down to the sun toward the east" — what the law forbade: see the sun, the moon and the stars… and be drawn away and bow down to them (Deuteronomy 4:19). They stand between the porch and the altar, at the door of the house itself, and turn their backs on it to do it.

  • v17 "They are putting the branch to their nose" — zemorah, a vine branch. What the act was is not known; the Greek has they are like people sneering. It ends the list of what was done in the temple.

speech.text: Ezekiel 8

And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was sitting in my house with the elders of Judah sitting before me, that the hand of the Lord GOD fell on me there.
I looked: a likeness like the appearance of a man. From the appearance of His waist downward was fire, and from His waist upward something like the appearance of brightness, like the gleam of amber.

He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my head; and the spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the seat of the image of jealousy was, which provokes jealousy.
The glory of the God of Israel was there, like the vision I had seen in the plain.
He said to me, "Son of man, lift up your eyes toward the north." So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and north of the altar gate, at the entrance, was this image of jealousy.

He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they are doing, the great detestable things the house of Israel is committing here, to drive Me far from My sanctuary? But you will see still greater detestable things."
He brought me to the entrance of the court, and I looked: there was a hole in the wall.
He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and there was a doorway.
He said to me, "Go in, and see the evil detestable things they are doing here."
So I went in and looked: carved on the wall all around were every form of creeping thing and loathsome beast, and all the idols of the house of Israel.

Seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel were standing before them, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them, each with his censer in his hand, and the fragrance of the cloud of incense was rising.

He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in his room of images? For they say, 'The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.'"
He said to me, "You will see still greater detestable things that they are doing."
He brought me to the entrance of the gate of the house of the LORD that faces north, and there sat women weeping for Tammuz.
He said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? You will see still greater detestable things than these."

He brought me into the inner court of the house of the LORD, and at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, and they were bowing down to the sun toward the east.

He said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? Is it too light a thing for the house of Judah to commit the detestable things they have committed here, that they must also fill the land with violence and provoke Me again and again? They are putting the branch to their nose.
So I, too, will act in wrath; My eye will not spare, and I will have no pity. Though they cry in My ears with a loud voice, I will not listen to them."
